note: Substrate §4.1 step 5 — 'UTF-16 string ordering', and the one case that actually tells UTF-16 code-unit order apart from Unicode code-point order. The axis keys are `zz\uFFFF` (single code unit 0xFFFF) and `zz\u{10000}` (surrogate pair 0xD800 0xDC00). By CODE POINT, U+FFFF < U+10000, so a code-point sorter emits `zz\uFFFF` first. By CODE UNIT, 0xD800 < 0xFFFF, so JCS emits `zz\u{10000}` first. Every canonicalizer that sorts by code point instead of code unit fails exactly here and nowhere else — which is why this fixture exists. The nested `annotations` object adds the ASCII case-order check: `A`(0x41) and `B`(0x42) precede `a`(0x61) and `b`(0x62), whereas a locale-aware comparator interleaves them.
